articles.summary_long:
Martian dust is a major hurdle for human missions to Mars. Like Moon dust, its fine size and electrostatically charged nature allow it to stick to spacesuits, metal, and just about any other surface they come into contact with. Dust storms are also common on Mars, ranging from small whirlwinds that happen daily to global dust storms that occur once every 3 Martian years (~5.5 Earth years) and envelop the entire planet.

In summary, the results showed that Martian dust may be less likely to be abrasive to equipment or harmful to astronaut health than lunar regolith. In addition, Martian dust can be exceptionally fine, with some ultrafine particles measuring as little as 100 nanometers (nm) in diameter. With Martian dust carrying perchlorates and other toxins, the health risk is magnified.

articles.title: A Stellar Odd Couple at an Unusual Stage of Evolution
articles.summary: They're main sequence stars like our Sun, meaning they're doing what most people probably think stars do: shining as they fuse hydrogen atoms into helium atoms on a vast scale. But some neutron stars do announce their presence as pulsars .
articles.summary_short: They're main sequence stars like our Sun, meaning they're doing what most people probably think stars do: shining as they fuse hydrogen atoms into helium atoms on a vast scale. But some neutron stars do announce their presence as pulsars .
articles.summary_long:
Most of the stars in the Milky Way are what we might call normal stars. They're main sequence stars like our Sun, meaning they're doing what most people probably think stars do: shining as they fuse hydrogen atoms into helium atoms on a vast scale. They form when massive stars explode as core-collapse supernovae.

Since massive stars are rare, so are neutron stars. But some neutron stars do announce their presence as pulsars . *Somewhere in this globular cluster (NGC 362), a millisecond pulsar and its binary companion, a white dwarf, are in a rare stage of evolution.

The pulsar, which is a dense, rapidly spinning neutron star, has been drawing material away from its less dense white dwarf companion, hastening its evolution into a white dwarf. It's a proto-white dwarf, which indicates that it's only just entering the earliest stages of becoming a white dwarf. This material was likely expelled during the mass-transfer phase, emphasizing how young the white dwarf is.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 10 – Saturn Behind the Moon
articles.summary: Explanation: Sometimes Saturn disappears. The bright dot near Saturn is not a moon of Saturn , but rather the star 85 Aquarii , which is further behind Saturn than Saturn is behind the Moon.
articles.summary_short: Explanation: Sometimes Saturn disappears. The bright dot near Saturn is not a moon of Saturn , but rather the star 85 Aquarii , which is further behind Saturn than Saturn is behind the Moon.
articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Sometimes Saturn disappears. It doesn't really go away, of course -- it just disappears from our view when Earth's Moon moves in front.

Such a Saturn ian eclipse, more formally called an occultation , was visible in early 2025 along a small swath of Earth -- from Greenland through central Europe and into northern Africa . The featured image is a digital fusion of three images, the first of just Saturn before it disappeared, and then two more of the Moon with different exposure lengths. The images were taken from Sardinia , Italy , after sunset.

The bright dot near Saturn is not a moon of Saturn , but rather the star 85 Aquarii , which is further behind Saturn than Saturn is behind the Moon. The next time the Moon moves in front of Saturn, as visible from some place on Earth , will be in 2031.

articles.summary: Mars Science Laboratory Mission Team Members By Remington Free, Operations Systems Engineer, NASA-JPL Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026 Today’s plan covered 3 sols, 5060, 5061, and 5062, as we take a few recharging sols before getting back to our normal drilling activities.

articles.summary_long:
Mars Science Laboratory Mission Team Members By Remington Free, Operations Systems Engineer, NASA-JPL Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026 Today’s plan covered 3 sols, 5060, 5061, and 5062, as we take a few recharging sols before getting back to our normal drilling activities. In any case, those activities are very power-hungry for our rover!

So today’s plan purposefully did not have a lot of activities in it so we could get a nice few power positive sols before we get back to drilling. Each of our three sols had a standard morning science block, with an extra exciting brand-new activity on 5061 (more on that shortly!). On 5061, we also conducted a brand-new engineering activity to test parallelism over one of our downlink communications windows.

This is a test of one of those pairs – running our CheMin “Get Data” activity at the same time as we are sending data to one of our orbiters. CheMin Get Data is a high CPU activity which transfers science data from the instrument to our flight computers. Overall, it was an exciting plan full of great remote science as we wait to be able to wrap up our drill campaign.

articles.title: Florestine Perrault Collins Passed for White to Learn the Trade, Then Ran a Black Portrait Studio in New Orleans for Twenty-Nine Years
articles.summary: She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood.
articles.summary_short: She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood.
articles.summary_long:
Florestine Perrault was fourteen when she started earning money in photography, hired as a clerk, photo finisher, stationery embosser, and developer by white-owned studios in New Orleans and by the Eastman Kodak Company. She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She set up her own studio in the living room of her house on St.

In 1935, six years into the Depression, she moved again, to South Rampart Street, the commercial and cultural spine of Black New Orleans, and renamed the business Collins Studio after her second husband, Herbert Collins. She stayed on South Rampart for the rest of her working life. Counting from the parlor in 1920 to her retirement to Los Angeles in 1949, she ran her own studio for twenty-nine years, through the Depression and a world war, and the addresses tell you she was reading her market carefully the whole time.

She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood. No institution had collected her negatives or her business records, and there was no studio archive to transfer, because nobody had ever treated the studio as an archive. The address where she photographed Black New Orleans for the last fourteen years of her career is a parking lot.

articles.title: Why Your Specialization Doesn’t Start With Camera Skills
articles.summary: Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject.
articles.summary_short: Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject.
articles.summary_long:
Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject. The subject determines the area they work in.

A person does not become suited to working with people because they chose portrait photography. They end up in portrait photography and stay there because they are able to work with people. Sports photography does not make a photographer fast or resistant to pressure; a person with these qualities is able to work in sports photography for years.

What, then, do ten years in one specialization mean? Ten years in certain working conditions and around a certain subject. They are better prepared to work with a certain subject and under certain conditions.

Elle en parlera le samedi 21 novembre à 16 h au Pôle socioculturel. Les 16 sites du festival s’étendent de Montier-en-Der à Giffaumont-Champaubert , en passant par Ceffonds, Droyes, Louze, Saint-Dizier et Vitry-le-François. En extérieur, le festival accueille Endangered de Tim Flach , portraits d’espèces menacées présentés par le Festival de la Camargue.

Enfin, l’Abbatiale accueille comme chaque année les images du concours international du festival. Ce concours reste l’un des temps forts du festival. Plusieurs soirées se détachent au Pôle socioculturel de Montier-en-Der.

articles.title: Son Lux’s Music Video for ‘Out Into Us’ Is an Atmospheric Foray Between Past and Present
articles.summary: Son Lux ’s newest music video is an atmospheric mini-epic. Last month, the video premiered at MASS MoCA —the piece is a joint commission by the museum and Pioneer Works and made in collaboration with Alex Cook —as an immersive, 17-minute installation titled “Out Into Us (Slow Down),” complementing the release of the band’s ninth studio album.

Last month, the video premiered at MASS MoCA —the piece is a joint commission by the museum and Pioneer Works and made in collaboration with Alex Cook —as an immersive, 17-minute installation titled “Out Into Us (Slow Down),” complementing the release of the band’s ninth studio album.
articles.summary_long:
Son Lux ’s newest music video is an atmospheric mini-epic. Last month, the video premiered at MASS MoCA —the piece is a joint commission by the museum and Pioneer Works and made in collaboration with Alex Cook —as an immersive, 17-minute installation titled “Out Into Us (Slow Down),” complementing the release of the band’s ninth studio album. “In the last decade, social media has created a reality in which music is often eclipsed by visuals, served up in an endless buffet of bite-sized and contextless flavors,” says a statement.

Portraying a multigenerational family seated around a table and passing the time in one another’s company, the video transports us back at least a century as scenes of a giant dust cloud evoke the Dust Bowl. Cook conjures tension, atmosphere, and moments of disrupted reality in a slippage of past and present. The Dust Bowl itself was inherently linked to an intense period when homesteaders, dreaming of prosperous lives for themselves, plowed vast swaths of prairie for their farms.

These bucolic tableaux and their romantic ideals could even be said to have functioned something like social media does today, as a way to spread information. “Sound can create a sanctuary—a space in which we can remember what it feels like to be present in our bodies and lost in our thoughts,” says the band’s guitarist, Rafiq Bhatia. “When you decrease the playback speed of a piece of music, you can really linger in its hidden corners and shadows: passing tensions and moments of release become whole rooms you can step into and stay for a while.”

articles.title: Caribbean Surrealism and Ancestral Memory Merge in Kelly Sinnapah Mary’s Lush Portraits
articles.summary: Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. Born in the French Caribbean territory of Guadeloupe, the artist conjures the mythic stories of her home through surreal scenes in which humans, flora, and fauna find a sort of hybrid harmony.
articles.summary_short: Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. Born in the French Caribbean territory of Guadeloupe, the artist conjures the mythic stories of her home through surreal scenes in which humans, flora, and fauna find a sort of hybrid harmony.
articles.summary_long:
Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. Born in the French Caribbean territory of Guadeloupe, the artist conjures the mythic stories of her home through surreal scenes in which humans, flora, and fauna find a sort of hybrid harmony. Sinnapah Mary’s recurring figure is named Sanbras, which the artist derived from a derogatory children’s book popular in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Through uncanny compositions that rely heavily on saturated color and delicate, organic textures, Sanbras appears as a subversive figure who morphs across various bodies of work and nods to the artist’s enduring questions: how relationships between all living beings manifest and the ways political forces—European colonialism and anthropocentrism, in particular—shape such connections. Melding various forms of knowledge and cultural symbols is a central part of Sinnapah Mary’s work, which emerges from her own evolving understanding of her family history. How a familial history informs one’s understanding of place and identity appears in the tender portraits of The Book of Violette , which is named after artist’s grandmother.

Often centering on lone protagonists, this series unfolds through folklore and references to the ways ancestral memory is passed through generations. Sinnapah Mary has described her grandmother’s magical garden of medicinal plants, for example, which appears as luscious flowers with human heads sprout from a plaid coverlet in “Violette’s Garden: My Father’s Shoes.” Holding a book with gilded pages and smoking a pipe, the schoolgirl stares at the viewer with a third eye, a symbol of wisdom and spiritual connection in Hinduism. Save the date for Sinnapah Mary’s Between earth and sea opening in February at The Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum in Ridgefield, Connecticut.

articles.title: Amy Liu Explores Light and Dark through Glitz, Mystique, and Opera
articles.summary: Not unlike the way a pearl grows inside a mollusk, wherein an irritant or parasite is gradually coated in a mineral called nacre, Amy Liu ’s paintings comprise layers of oil pigment over underpaintings. This preparation technique dates to the early Renaissance, its first use attributed to Jan van Eyck, who added a monochrome glaze to the surface of panels to establish tonal values before building up the picture.
articles.summary_short: Not unlike the way a pearl grows inside a mollusk, wherein an irritant or parasite is gradually coated in a mineral called nacre, Amy Liu ’s paintings comprise layers of oil pigment over underpaintings. This preparation technique dates to the early Renaissance, its first use attributed to Jan van Eyck, who added a monochrome glaze to the surface of panels to establish tonal values before building up the picture.
articles.summary_long:
Not unlike the way a pearl grows inside a mollusk, wherein an irritant or parasite is gradually coated in a mineral called nacre, Amy Liu ’s paintings comprise layers of oil pigment over underpaintings. This preparation technique dates to the early Renaissance, its first use attributed to Jan van Eyck, who added a monochrome glaze to the surface of panels to establish tonal values before building up the picture. In her solo exhibition Pearled Chiaroscuro at Harper’s , Liu taps into the Renaissance in more ways than one.

Liu focuses on women wearing embellished gowns and draped in elaborate jewelry, with an emphasis on pearls. She also invokes the spirit of a night at opera, drawing on her own background as a trained soprano. Rather than highlighting the identities of the figures, whether performers or spectators, the artist focuses on their elaborate and luxurious garments.

By concealing the women’s identities and viewing them through their sartorial choices, Liu explores how high fashion is a channel of not only status but one’s sense of self, where in turn, the garments literally and figuratively mask the person wearing them. “Figures are abstracted and their identities deliberately concealed, as if supporting the ornamentation rather than the other way around,” the gallery says. Pearled Chiaroscuro continues through December 19 at Harper’s Apartment on the Upper East Side, New York City.

articles.title: Qubole : des accès cloud oubliés exposent les entreprises au vol de données
articles.summary: Des attaquants ont détourné les accès AWS de Qubole pour voler des secrets et des données chez plusieurs entreprises clientes. Des attaquants non identifiés ont utilisé des identifiants compromis associés au compte AWS de Qubole pour s’introduire dans les environnements cloud de plusieurs clients.
articles.summary_short: Des attaquants ont détourné les accès AWS de Qubole pour voler des secrets et des données chez plusieurs entreprises clientes. Des attaquants non identifiés ont utilisé des identifiants compromis associés au compte AWS de Qubole pour s’introduire dans les environnements cloud de plusieurs clients.
articles.summary_long:
Des attaquants ont détourné les accès AWS de Qubole pour voler des secrets et des données chez plusieurs entreprises clientes. Certaines avaient abandonné la plateforme sans révoquer ses autorisations. Des attaquants non identifiés ont utilisé des identifiants compromis associés au compte AWS de Qubole pour s’introduire dans les environnements cloud de plusieurs clients.

Des identifiants associés au compte AWS de Qubole ont alors servi à appeler l’API sts afin d’obtenir des identifiants temporaires correspondant aux rôles d’intégration gérés par les clients. Les appels provenaient du compte AWS 805246085872 et utilisaient l’identifiant IAM AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS. Les opérations se sont poursuivies le 15 octobre.

L’activité a duré jusqu’au 26 octobre 2026. Une fois dans les environnements clients, les attaquants ont exploré plusieurs services AWS. Les chercheurs ont également repéré une autre campagne, entre le 8 et le 11 octobre, exploitant des clés AWS appartenant aux clients pour des intégrations Qubole.

articles.title: NIS 2 : la loi Résilience arrive enfin à l’Assemblée
articles.summary: Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné en séance publique après plusieurs reports. Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné à l’Assemblée nationale du 9 au 13 novembre.
articles.summary_short: Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné en séance publique après plusieurs reports. Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné à l’Assemblée nationale du 9 au 13 novembre.
articles.summary_long:
Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné en séance publique après plusieurs reports. Son adoption doit permettre de préciser le cadre réglementaire applicable aux milliers d’organisations concernées. Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné à l’Assemblée nationale du 9 au 13 novembre.

Présenté en Conseil des ministres le 15 octobre 2024, le projet de loi relatif à la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité a été adopté par le Sénat en mars 2025, puis à l’unanimité par la commission spéciale de l’Assemblée nationale en septembre de la même année. Le nombre de secteurs couverts passe de 6 à 18, et celui des organisations concernées de quelques centaines à près de 15 000, réparties entre entités essentielles et entités importantes. Les entités essentielles s’exposent à des amendes pouvant atteindre 10 M€ ou 2 % de leur chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial.

Pour les entités importantes, le plafond est fixé à 7 M€ ou 1,4 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial. Cette disposition oppose deux approches de la sécurité. Anne Le Hénanff, ministre déléguée chargée de l’Intelligence artificielle et du Numérique, le considère comme un cavalier législatif, autrement dit une disposition sans lien suffisamment direct avec l’objet du projet de loi.

articles.title: Robotique et IA physique : les fabricants de puces défendent les atouts européens
articles.summary: Infineon, STMicroelectronics et NXP estiment que l’Europe peut rivaliser avec les États-Unis et l’Asie dans la robotique et l’IA physique. Leurs dirigeants misent sur l’expérience du continent dans l’automobile, l’industrie et la conception de systèmes sûrs.
articles.summary_short: Infineon, STMicroelectronics et NXP estiment que l’Europe peut rivaliser avec les États-Unis et l’Asie dans la robotique et l’IA physique. Leurs dirigeants misent sur l’expérience du continent dans l’automobile, l’industrie et la conception de systèmes sûrs.
articles.summary_long:
Infineon, STMicroelectronics et NXP estiment que l’Europe peut rivaliser avec les États-Unis et l’Asie dans la robotique et l’IA physique. Leurs dirigeants misent sur l’expérience du continent dans l’automobile, l’industrie et la conception de systèmes sûrs. L’Europe dispose des compétences nécessaires pour rivaliser avec les États-Unis et l’Asie dans la robotique et l’IA physique, estiment les dirigeants d’Infineon, de STMicroelectronics et de NXP.

Réunis à Munich le 9 novembre, ils ont mis en avant l’expérience du continent dans l’automobile et les technologies industrielles, rapporte Reuters . « Pour moi, l’IA industrielle ou IA physique est avant tout un enjeu que l’Europe se doit de remporter », a déclaré Jochen Hanebeck, directeur général d’Infineon. Selon ces dirigeants, l’arrivée de l’IA dans les véhicules, les robots et les machines industrielles soutiendra la demande de composants fiables.

Jean-Marc Chéry, directeur général de STMicroelectronics, souligne la nécessité de rapprocher fabricants et clients, notamment pour entraîner les robots dans des environnements simulés. Pour Rafael Sotomayor, directeur général de NXP, les compétences historiques européennes constituent un avantage dans la conception de systèmes sûrs. Lorsque l’IA passe de la recommandation à l’action physique, les conséquences d’une erreur peuvent devenir irréversibles.

articles.title: L’Europe lance un plan de 525 M€ pour aider les start-up qui conçoivent des puces
articles.summary: L’Europe veut reprendre la main sur la conception des puces. Le 4 novembre 2026, la Commission européenne a officiellement lancé la European Chip Design Platform, une initiative dotée de 525 M€.
articles.summary_short: L’Europe veut reprendre la main sur la conception des puces. Le 4 novembre 2026, la Commission européenne a officiellement lancé la European Chip Design Platform, une initiative dotée de 525 M€.
articles.summary_long:
L’Europe veut reprendre la main sur la conception des puces. Le 4 novembre 2026, la Commission européenne a officiellement lancé la European Chip Design Platform, une initiative dotée de 525 M€. La plateforme européenne doit justement faciliter cet accès.

Les 85 M€ restants financeront l’infrastructure cloud de la plateforme, les services d’accompagnement et le développement d’outils de conception open source. Pour Bruxelles, renforcer les capacités européennes de conception est indispensable pour offrir davantage de débouchés aux infrastructures de production installées sur le continent. La Commission européenne considère que le développement d’un écosystème de concepteurs locaux créera une demande supplémentaire pour les capacités industrielles européennes.

L’objectif initial était notamment de porter à 20 % d’ici à 2030 la part de l’Union européenne dans la production mondiale de puces. La European Chip Design Platform sera opérée par un consortium conduit par l’institut belge de recherche imec, avec le soutien de l’entreprise commune européenne consacrée aux semi-conducteurs (Chips Joint Undertaking). Le réseau européen de centres de compétences dans les semi-conducteurs doit également aider à orienter les entreprises vers les dispositifs de soutien disponibles.

articles.title: Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
articles.summary: We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford.
articles.summary_short: We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford.
articles.summary_long:
Vital to almost all life as we know it, oxygen has long been valued as a tracer of the chemical evolution of the of the cosmos. As such, it provides a practical means of tracing how the heavy elements of iron, carbon, nickel, magnesium and sulfur --- the real building blocks of habitable planets like our own --- are distributed throughout the galaxy and beyond. For the first time, we have measured both how much oxygen produced by stars in low-mass galaxies remains in those galaxies, and how much oxygen has been lost from those galaxies throughout their lifetimes, Grace Telford, the paperâs second author and an assistant professor at the University of Utahâs Dept.

The findings show that dwarf galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by stars, says NASA. We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. The explanation is that energetic radiation from massive stars and their deaths as supernovae drive oxygen-rich gas out of the galaxies over time, she says.

Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford. In low-mass galaxies like those in the GLOW project, that value is more like one oxygen atom for every 10,000-20,000 hydrogen atoms, she says. The GLOW project found that low-mass galaxies lose more oxygen than current galaxy formation simulations predict, implying that we donât yet have a complete understanding of how massive stars interact with their host galaxies, says Telford.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 9 – Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
articles.summary: Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch?
articles.summary_short: Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch?
articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula's shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch's head.

Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to -- because it has been partly eroded by -- the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image .

The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel's intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth's daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth's atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen .

The ozone hole ranked seventh largest by area in 48 years of monitoring, but it was not as deep as other large holes on record. This story is an update to the Antarctic ozone hole feature in our World of Change series , which documents how Earth changes over months, seasons, and years. NASA satellite instruments revealed the continental scale of this Antarctic ozone thinning, and it came to be known as the ozone hole.

Red and yellow areas indicate the ozone hole. These maps show the state of the ozone hole each year on the day of maximum depth—the day the lowest ozone concentrations were measured. The deepest ozone hole occurred in 1994, when concentrations fell to just 73 DU on September 30.

In the early years of the 21st century, annual ozone holes roughly stabilized (see NASA Ozone Watch for annual averages). Human-produced bromine compounds, which are far less abundant but much more destructive to ozone, also contribute to the Antarctic ozone hole. articles.title: 7 Everyday Habits That Quietly Damage Your Camera Gear
articles.summary: A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. Those small habits stack up over years of shooting, and changing them costs far less than replacing glass.
articles.summary_short: A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. articles.summary_long:
A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. Those small habits stack up over years of shooting, and changing them costs far less than replacing glass. The first is carrying the camera mounted on the tripod, legs extended, over your shoulder.

Put the hood on, flip the rig so the lens points down, and use an L-bracket or a plate with anti-rotation pins, since a single-screw plate lets the camera spin and swing the lens into a leg or a rock. His approach is to seal the camera in a Ziploc bag before the transition, then let it warm up inside the bag before taking it out. Carry a camera from 20°F air into a heated cabin, and the moisture in the indoor air condenses on the cold body and inside the lens.

The bag trick works in both directions, as long as you seal the camera in the air it's currently sitting in before you change environments. Weather sealing, he points out, isn't waterproofing, and no shot is worth leaving an uncovered camera on a tripod in a shower. Most of his own mishaps happened that way, from lens hoods dropped off cliffs to lens caps dropped in the water.

articles.title: The Story of One of the Most Famous Photos Ever
articles.summary: The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped.
articles.summary_short: The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped.
articles.summary_long:
In January 1996, Charles O'Rear pulled onto the shoulder of California State Route 121 in southern Sonoma County, pushed a Mamiya RZ67 through a wire fence, and made a few exposures of a bare green hill. The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. Two years later, that frame was sitting on a Corbis stock catalog disc as image 71810, with a copyright bar across the bottom reading "©CHARLES O'REAR/Westlight 71810WL." The popular version puts the picture in Napa Valley.

The hill O'Rear photographed had been cleared years earlier for the same reason. In a 2010 interview, he measured his frame against Ansel Adams. CNET wrote in 2014 that Microsoft cropped the picture and pumped up the green, and the Napa Valley Register wrote the same year that Microsoft had admitted to darkening the green hill.

What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped. Same clouds, same hill, same wispy cirrus in the upper left, nothing moved. In 2000, the XP team reached O'Rear through Corbis, and they did not want a license.

Dustin Abbott puts the Swift 40mm up against three 40mm lenses he has already reviewed: the Sony FE 40mm f/2.5 G , the Viltrox AF 40mm f/2.5 , and the Nikon NIKKOR Z 40mm f/2 .

At $798, the Sony is a lot of money for an f/2.5 lens. The Sirui comes in Sony E, Nikon Z, L-mount, and Fujifilm X versions, and Abbott tested it on Sony. Minimum focus is 40 cm for 0.14x magnification, which Abbott calls about average and below what the Sony and Nikon manage.

Focus breathing is noticeable, and because this is a third-party lens, Sony's in-camera breathing compensation can't correct it. He liked it enough to agree to review the other new Swift lens, a 20mm f/2.4. If the fringing worries you, the frost crystals Abbott shoots partway through the video show exactly how much of it to expect.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: The sky glows with soft pinkish colors of fading twilight in this serendipitous mountaintop vista. Taken in subfreezing temperatures, the thoughtfully composed photo shows snowy, rugged peaks seen from a mountain pass on 2017 November 14.

Below lies the village of La Villa, Alta Badia in Italy 's Dolomite Alps . Above the nestled village lights, the constellation Ursa Major hangs over the northern horizon. But most stunning is the intense fireball meteor.

It was captured during the camera's exposure by chance as it flashed east to west across the northern horizon, under Ursa Major's familiar Big Dipper asterism . Sightings of this major fireball meteor were widely reported in European skies, making it one of the most reported fireball events ever for planet Earth's American Meteor Society and the International Meteor Organization . The meteor's measured track over Germany is consistent with its origin near the active radiant of November's Northern Taurid Meteor Shower , a shower associated with dust from Encke's comet .

articles.title: The 3 Camera Modes One Wedding Photographer Uses for Every Portrait
articles.summary: After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.
articles.summary_short: After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.
articles.summary_long:
Manual mode has a reputation as the serious way to shoot portraits, and plenty of people switch to it the moment they feel comfortable with their camera. Outdoors, with clouds drifting across the sun and subjects walking in and out of shade, that habit can leave you chasing exposure instead of watching your subject. After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed.

The mode choice rests on a simple idea he lays out early: "ISO gives you headroom in low light, and shutter speed gives you headroom in bright light." On a sunny day, your ISO is probably already sitting between 100 and 400, close to the floor, so it has nowhere left to go. That's where manual with auto ISO falls apart in daylight: at f/1.2 or f/1.4, the camera slams into ISO 100, the image starts blowing out, and you're back to turning the shutter dial yourself. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.

Castein skips the auto setting because shutter speed, more than aperture or ISO, decides whether he gets the picture at all, and he treats in-body stabilization as if it isn't there, since it steadies the camera and does nothing for a subject who moves. Under 1/125 s, he takes a lot more, and slower than that, he asks people to hold still or, in his words, to "move in slow motion." The setting pays off in noise, too: at an outdoor cafe in open shade, a 1/1,000 s minimum had his ISO at 3,200, and because his subjects were sitting still, lowering it to 1/500 s brought the ISO straight down to 1,600. Night is when he goes back to manual with auto ISO, since ISO has the headroom in the dark, and he warns that many cameras will drop below your minimum shutter speed once auto ISO hits its limit.

Starting on manufacturer paper removes that whole layer of setup, so when a print comes out too dark or with a color cast, you can trace it to your file, your print settings, or your monitor. The same profiles also drive soft proofing in Lightroom and Photoshop, letting you preview on screen how an image will translate to a given paper before you spend a sheet.

If you can't get a clean, good-looking version of that file onto basic manufacturer paper, he asks what hope you have of judging whether some other paper is better. He wants you to treat the print as the end point of your editing workflow. That's also why he won't name a favorite: his pick suits his images, and you need to print enough to find your own.

articles.title: Why Focusing on the Background Makes Photos Feel Dreamy
articles.summary: Nearly everything you learn about focus points in one direction: keep the subject sharp and let the background fall apart. The out-of-focus subject reaches a similar mood using nothing but where you place your focus point, which means you can try it on your next outing with whatever is already in your bag.
articles.summary_short: Nearly everything you learn about focus points in one direction: keep the subject sharp and let the background fall apart. The out-of-focus subject reaches a similar mood using nothing but where you place your focus point, which means you can try it on your next outing with whatever is already in your bag.
articles.summary_long:
Nearly everything you learn about focus points in one direction: keep the subject sharp and let the background fall apart. Reversing that, so the person in front of the lens goes soft while the scene behind them stays crisp, is one of the simplest ways to make an image feel dreamy and a little unreal. The first choice is how you get focus onto the background.

Manual focus is the most direct route: set the lens on the scene behind your subject, keep the subject in the foreground, and shoot. If you use the AF lock approach, switching to a single small focus point and turning subject detection off makes the camera far more cooperative, and assigning detection to a custom button lets you toggle it in a second. Back-button focus solves a similar problem from another angle.

Once focus is separated from the shutter button, you can set it on the background, release, and the camera won't refocus on your subject when you half-press to shoot. The out-of-focus subject reaches a similar mood using nothing but where you place your focus point, which means you can try it on your next outing with whatever is already in your bag. On a wider lens, you may need a lower f-number, and at something like 100mm, he suggests trying f/5.6.

articles.summary: La collection 100 photos pour la liberté de la presse , publiée par Reporters sans frontières, s’enrichit d’un nouvel album. Robert Doisneau naît le 14 avril 1912 à Gentilly.

articles.summary_long:
La collection 100 photos pour la liberté de la presse , publiée par Reporters sans frontières, s’enrichit d’un nouvel album. Celui-ci porte un autre regard sur l’œuvre de Robert Doisneau , en mettant en lumière son enthousiasme communicatif pour les gens et les scènes du quotidien. Vingt-six ans séparent le premier album de RSF consacré à Robert Doisneau (n° 9, avril 2000) de ce nouveau volume, paru cet automne.

Robert Doisneau naît le 14 avril 1912 à Gentilly. Les années 1950 marquent le pinacle de sa carrière . Dans les années 1970, il continue d’immortaliser le « vieux Paris », qui disparaît peu à peu.

Les années 1980 sont celles de la consécration (Grand Prix national de la photographie en 1983, prix Balzac en 1986) et de la redécouverte de son œuvre au travers de plusieurs monographies. » fait l’éloge de l’école buissonnière, emblème d’un « apprentissage de la liberté », et pose un regard tendre et amusé sur la jeunesse des années 1950. Lui qui a longtemps partagé les réticences de son père, photographe, envers l’œuvre de Doisneau, y voit aujourd’hui une « jubilation devant la douceur du monde » .

articles.title: Abstract Wool Compositions Cascade from Weathered Metal in Amine El Gotaibi’s Sculptures
articles.summary: It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place.
articles.summary_short: It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place.
articles.summary_long:
It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place. El Gotaibi’s most recent body of work is on view this month at Southern Guild .

Presented in an exhibition titled Wind From the North , a suite of sculptures made of metal and wool speak to the tensions between the land and the state and the ways we mark change. Affixed to these aged backdrops are tufts of beige and rust-colored fibers, which are either wound into tightly knotted tufts or left free-flowing. Echoing the undulating terrain of mountains and the countryside, the cascading fibers tether to the artist’s interest in examining the landscapes of his home country and Northern Africa, more broadly.

For El Gotaibi, this material significance directly links to his desire to challenge the idea that Africa’s cultural contributions are most likely to emerge from the central and south. Instead, Wind from the North , an exhibition statement says, “extends this proposition beyond fixed coordinates, imagining geography as porous and interconnected, shaped as much by what passes through it as by the lines drawn around it.” Wind From the North is on view through January 9 in New York. Find more from El Gotaibi on Instagram .

An accessible antidote to generative AI, Arkivism is a new public domain index that catalogs millions of artworks, illustrations, photos, video, and more from dozens of museums and archives around the world.

articles.title: What Else Could It Mean? A Book Surveys the Playful, Iconoclastic Works of James Wines
articles.summary: An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean?
articles.summary_short: An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean?
articles.summary_long:
It’s not uncommon for artists and architects to espouse a desire for breaking conventions and pushing boundaries, but so few have embodied such a mandate as James Wines. An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. No matter the project, SITE’s approach is rooted in questioning the division between art and architecture and defying expectations.

In the preface to the new book, What Else Could It Mean? , Wines describes how he spent months in Rome after college soaking in the religious designs and civically unified architecture, which inspired what became his signature mode of working. “What else could it mean?” became a driving ethos that centered around “architecture as a critique of itself, as an inversion of design expectations, as humorous insights and the absorption of context as a motivating source of ideas,” he writes.

Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean? showcases dozens of projects from the SITE oeuvre. The BEST designs are just a piece of SITE’s broader commentary on commercialization.

Trois de ses sites ont subi une modification à distance des paramètres de leurs chambres froides, via un prestataire. Aucun produit sanguin n'a toutefois été perdu ou altéré. Dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre, une cyberattaque visant un prestataire de l'Établissement français du sang (EFS) a entraîné une modification des paramètres de fonctionnement de chambres froides sur trois de ses sites.

L'incident a été confirmé le 3 novembre par l'établissement. Selon son communiqué, des anomalies ont affecté les installations de supervision et de pilotage des équipements frigorifiques. Les équipements concernés servent notamment à conserver des poches de plasma destinées aux transfusions ou au fractionnement pour la fabrication de médicaments.

L'attaque a touché un prestataire chargé de ses installations frigorifiques. Cet incident intervient dans un contexte marqué par plusieurs attaques visant des équipements frigorifiques en Europe. Une nouvelle vague d'incidents a également touché plusieurs pays européens au début du mois de novembre .

L'entreprise SpaceX, propriété d'Elon Musk, a choisi les plateformes Dragonwing de Qualcomm pour construire son futur réseau mobile 5G aux Etats-Unis. Le 4 novembre 2026, Qualcomm a annoncé avoir été retenu pour fournir les technologies qui équiperont le futur réseau terrestre 5G de Starlink Mobile aux Etats-Unis.

Pour cette infrastructure, SpaceX s'appuiera sur deux plateformes de Qualcomm Technologies, Dragonwing QRU100 et QDU100. Qualcomm met également en avant les gains attendus en matière de couverture, de capacité et d'efficacité énergétique. Selon Qualcomm, cette approche doit notamment contribuer à augmenter les capacités du réseau tout en maîtrisant la consommation énergétique des équipements.

Qualcomm fournira les composants et les logiciels nécessaires au traitement radio et à la couche physique. SpaceX conservera de son côté la maîtrise des autres éléments de l'architecture réseau, notamment les couches logicielles supérieures. Le contrat porte néanmoins, à ce stade, sur le déploiement d'un réseau terrestre 5G.

After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia .

The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite's Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope . Swift had a combination of instruments, including an X-ray telescope and a gamma-ray telescope , that worked together to enable humanity to study, in unprecedented detail, the fastest and most energetic explosions in the universe. The most recent solar maximum accelerated the decay of the satellite's orbit.

An innovative mission to rescue Swift by boosting its orbit was not successful . Swift burned on reentry like a shooting star, but the impressive data acquired by the telescope over its mission will continue to bring light to the mysteries of the cosmos for years to come. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science.

articles.summary_long:
Annoncé en septembre, le firmware 2.00 de la Nikon ZR a été détaillé par Nikon le 3 novembre. Au programme : le Log3G10 en H.265 , un réglage de la réduction du bruit, le focus peaking en R3D NE et plus de personnalisation. La v2.00 va plus loin, et Nikon la présente comme la première mise à jour majeure de la caméra.

En Log3G10 comme en N-Log, on peut choisir parmi quatre niveaux de réduction du bruit en haute sensibilité. Côté mise au point, le focus peaking arrive enfin en R3D NE, y compris quand un LUT 3D est appliqué. Nikon n’annonce en revanche aucune évolution de l’autofocus avec cette version.

En septembre, Nikon avait aussi indiqué que RED mettait à jour ses applications de pilotage à distance RED Control et RED Control Pro pour les rendre compatibles avec la ZR. Nikon annonce que le firmware 2.00 sortira avant la fin de 2026 , sans date précise pour l’instant. Pour en savoir plus sur la caméra, retrouvez notre prise en main de la Nikon ZR et notre interview Nikon à l’IBC 2025 .

articles.summary_long:
Après une campagne Kickstarter qui a dépassé les espérances de ses créateurs, Mondo Robotics ouvre les ventes de Beni , un robot caméra sur roues capable de suivre son utilisateur et de le filmer en 4K , sans opérateur ni trépied. Contrairement aux drones à suivi automatique de DJI, Beni ne vole pas : il roule au sol, aux côtés de son sujet. Les premières livraisons sont annoncées à partir du 10 novembre 2026 , et le robot est proposé dès 841 dollars (environ 730 €) en prix de lancement pour la France.

Beni est le premier produit de Mondo Robotics , une jeune entreprise fondée en 2025 et basée à Hong Kong , qui revendique environ 150 ingénieurs et designers répartis entre Shenzhen et Palo Alto et une équipe en partie issue de DJI . Face à une caméra de poche stabilisée comme la DJI Osmo Pocket 4P et son double objectif, Beni apporte l’autonomie de déplacement , au prix d’un encombrement et d’un tarif bien supérieurs . Au-delà de son allure de petit robot de dessin animé, Beni embarque un module caméra comparable à celui des caméras de poche récentes.

Beni n’est pas étanche , Mondo Robotics le réserve donc aux usages par temps sec. Mondo Robotics, malgré une équipe en partie issue de chez DJI, en est à son premier produit . Peut-être que c’est celui-ci que l’équipe de Mondo Robotics a repris… Enfin, la législation reste floue.

articles.title: OpenAI dévoile GPT-6 Cyber
articles.summary: Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox.
articles.summary_short: Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox.
articles.summary_long:
Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox. Quelques jours après avoir dévoilé Image 2.6, la nouvelle version de son générateur d'images, OpenAI annonce GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et dérivé de GPT-6 Astra.

OpenAI poursuit le développement de ses capacités en cybersécurité avec GPT-6 Cyber, une déclinaison spécialisée de son modèle GPT-6 Astra. Les premiers résultats communiqués par OpenAI illustrent les capacités du modèle. Lors de travaux menés sur Firefox, GPT-6 Cyber a permis d’identifier 81 vulnérabilités inédites, classées de haute gravité par Mozilla.

Le modèle aurait permis de reproduire 1 724 vulnérabilités et de développer 948 exploits fonctionnels. OpenAI classe ce modèle au niveau « critique » en matière de cybersécurité, une première pour ses modèles Cyber. GPT-6 Cyber n’est donc pas proposé en accès libre.

On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight.

The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions.

“For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. NASA successfully demonstrated technology designed to help spacecraft autonomously navigate to safe landing sites on the Moon and on other planets. An Alta-X drone equipped with the agency’s Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution ( SPLICE ) guidance, navigation, and control payload completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers Aug. The flight took place at Rogers Dry Lake near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

During the tests, the SPLICE payload used an advanced guidance system to map the terrain and assess potential landing areas. If the system determines the targeted landing area is unsafe, the system diverts the drone to a safer location. “This flight test is the culmination of almost a decade of work, for the SPLICE project,” said Davis Adams, NASA project manager.

Validation of the guidance and navigation systems are applicable to terrestrial, lunar, and Martian descent and landing missions.” NASA has worked with a number of commercial lunar lander providers to implement iterations of SPLICE into their platforms. “Some of the companies also are evaluating the system’s navigation capabilities for precision landing applications, as well as potential extensions for autonomous surface mobility.” NASA’s Flight Opportunities project, based at NASA Armstrong, enabled flight testing of the SPLICE project early in its development that laid a foundation for it to continue advancing its technology readiness level to what it is today. Flight testing included both a descent altitude and a landing trajectory in 2019 similar to what is expected on a lunar mission and the demonstration of two NASA-developed precision landing sensor systems in 2020.

In the last week of December 2010, a railroad worker named Jim DeNike drove from Arkansas to Parsons, Kansas, and loaded a dozen boxes holding nearly 50,000 slides into an old maroon Pontiac. He had sent Dwayne's Photo 1,580 rolls of Kodachrome and paid $15,798 to have them developed, borrowing against his father's retirement account to cover it. Kodachrome died when one small lab in southeast Kansas went quiet, because a Kodachrome roll was not a color film in any sense a modern photographer would recognize.

Nearly every other color film you have shot carries its couplers inside the emulsion, waiting for oxidized developer to meet them and form dye in place. The yellow developer then builds yellow dye in the top layer. The middle green-sensitive layer gets no light at all.

The film only becomes a color film at the end of that chain, and the chain was scrapped in Parsons in January 2011. You can still find frozen Kodachrome on auction sites, and you can still shoot it. The one machine it cannot run is the one that made Kodachrome a color film, and there are 50,000 slides of trains in Arkansas that exist because one man got them to Kansas in time.

articles.title: High-Speed Sync vs. Global Shutter for Flash Portraits in Bright Sun
articles.summary: Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2.

articles.summary_long:
Shoot a flash portrait at f/1.2 in midday sun and you run into a wall fast: most cameras stop syncing with a flash somewhere around 1/160 to 1/250 s, and anything faster leaves dark bands across the frame. Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. The high-speed sync shots come from a Sony a7R VI with the Sony FE 50mm f/1.2 GM , because the Sony a9 III won't go into high-speed sync mode at all.

At f/1.2, the ceiling drops to 1/16,000 s, which is still far beyond what a focal plane shutter can sync at. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2. The logic carries over to leaf shutter cameras such as the Fujifilm X100VI , where the flash also fires as one burst at shutter speeds a focal plane shutter can't sync at.

On any camera, shutter speed sets how bright the background looks, and the flash sets how bright your subject looks. A global or leaf shutter lets you push those two apart much further. What the global shutter opens up for portraits is control over ambient light.

At the turn of the 20th century, art—especially the “high” mediums of painting and sculpture—were viewed and taught through the lens of deeply ingrained conventions about what made art good.

Avast déploie en France un VPN gratuit, sans publicité et utilisable sur un nombre illimité d'appareils. L'éditeur de cybersécurité mise sur une formule sans plafond de données pour se démarquer de ses concurrents, tout en réservant certaines fonctionnalités à son offre payante. Avast lance en France une nouvelle offre VPN gratuite, accessible sur Windows, macOS, Android et iOS.

Avast annonce également l'absence de publicité et de plafond mensuel de données. Avast propose aussi une fonctionnalité permettant de suspendre temporairement le VPN pendant 15, 30 ou 60 minutes. Les utilisateurs peuvent sélectionner trois emplacements de serveurs, contre davantage de destinations avec l'abonnement Avast Premium VPN.

L'éditeur indique également que sa formule gratuite propose des vitesses standard. La décision interdit notamment à Avast de vendre ou de concéder sous licence des données de navigation à des fins publicitaires. Le marché compte déjà des offres gratuites, notamment celle de Proton VPN.

articles.title: Assyria is Far from Ancient in Esther Elia’s Characterizations of Contemporary ‘Diasporic Deities’

articles.summary_short: Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken.
articles.summary_long:
Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. In the ancient Assyrian Empire, giant bulls or lions with human heads and wings represented the deities, which artisans often carved at a monumental scale to protect cities and palaces. For Albuquerque-based Esther Elia , who is of Assyrian and Irish descent, lamassu are anything but a relic of the distant past.

Through sculpture, paintings, and textiles, the artist explores contemporary Assyrian experience through pattern, fashion, and autobiography. Her solo exhibition, Bazaar Ashuraya at Hecho a Mano , centers around a new collection of acrylic paintings, plus tile mosaics and functional objects. Elia delves into the theme of home, where lamps, garments, and paintings evocative of rugs or tapestries portray vibrant figures, shapes, and objects associated with daily life.

“The home is where Assyria lives and breathes,” Elia says in a statement. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken. Even if we speak English or Arabic or Farsi or French or Swedish outside of the home, the home is where Assyrian food is made, where Assyrian customs thrive, and where culture is maintained as well as created—pushed forward.

His new book, Eight Seconds: Legacy in Motion , is an addendum to his earlier body of work with 91 new images that spotlight the people and places integral to Black rodeo culture. Published by Damiani , the updated edition features Texan teenager Kortnee Solomon, who’s captivated audiences as one of the youngest competitors, on the cover. articles.title: Les frigos des supermarchés européens victimes d'une nouvelle vague de cyberattaques
articles.summary: Après une première série de piratages en France en octobre, les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs enseignes européennes ont de nouveau été ciblés ce 2 novembre. Belgique, Suède, Irlande et plusieurs autres pays sont concernés.
articles.summary_short: Après une première série de piratages en France en octobre, les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs enseignes européennes ont de nouveau été ciblés ce 2 novembre. Belgique, Suède, Irlande et plusieurs autres pays sont concernés.
articles.summary_long:
Après une première série de piratages en France en octobre, les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs enseignes européennes ont de nouveau été ciblés ce 2 novembre. Belgique, Suède, Irlande et plusieurs autres pays sont concernés. Lundi 2 novembre, les installations frigorifiques de plusieurs supermarchés européens ont été manipulées à distance, provoquant des pertes de marchandises et des perturbations opérationnelles.

Plusieurs enseignes européennes ont signalé des dysfonctionnements de leurs équipements de réfrigération. En Belgique, une quarantaine de magasins Delhaize auraient été touchés, tandis que plusieurs points de vente Carrefour ont également signalé des incidents. Des magasins Intermarché et Spar figurent aussi parmi les établissements concernés.

La Suède et l'Irlande sont également affectées, l'enseigne ICA a confirmé des incidents dans plusieurs magasins, tandis qu'au moins treize supermarchés SuperValu ont confirmé la perte de produits frais et surgelés. Le Luxembourg, les Pays-Bas et l'Estonie figurent aussi parmi les pays concernés. Environ 700 magasins auraient été concernés par la compromission de leurs systèmes de réfrigération.

articles.summary_long:
Astrophysicists think that the supermassive black holes (SMBH) we see in the modern Universe are the result of a long drawn-out process. That process is referred to as the hierarchical black hole mergers framework. Some of the most massive appear to have billions of solar masses.

They either explode as supernovae, and their cores collapse, forming black holes, or they collapse directly into black holes. In between stellar mass black holes and SMBH are intermediate mass black holes (IMBH.) These black holes range in mass from about 100 solar masses to 100,000 solar masses. A 2020 paper presented the only direct evidence of an IMBH when the waves showed that two black holes, with 85 and 66 solar masses, merged to create an IMBH with about 142 solar masses.

Research titled " Massive star clusters detected by JWST as natural birth places to form intermediate-mass black holes " may have the answer. articles.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
articles.summary: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_short: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_long:
The Solar System's asteroids are sometimes referred to as fossils because they preserve evidence of the conditions when the Solar System formed. Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. Aqueous alteration isn't a rare action that happens only in space environments; it's common on Earth.

(Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration. There seems to be two components, each altered under a different set of aqueous conditions. An asteroid can be clumpy on a macroscale, but how can it have two components in the same mineral matrix?

They found the expected serpentine and saponite, but they also identified something else: poorly crystalline magnesium silicate hydrate (M-S-H). Much of their matrices could be poorly crystalline M-S-H. That sample should be on Earth five years from now.

articles.title: In 2013, Researchers Pulled Recognizable Faces of Bystanders Out of the Eye Reflections in a Portrait
articles.summary: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_short: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_long:
An anonymous peer reviewer worked through a manuscript, looked at one of its figures, and recognized one of the authors. The face was a reflection in another person's eye. The subject's face, hair excluded, took up about 12 million of them.

The iris took about 54,000, which the authors note is under 0.5% of frontal face area. Out of that iris, they cropped rectangles 27 to 36 pixels wide by 42 to 56 pixels high, framed head and shoulders like a tiny passport photo. Average face area inside those crops was 322 pixels.

At identical framing, a bystander crop that ran 27 to 36 pixels wide in 2013 comes out around 44 to 58 pixels wide today, and 322 pixels of face area becomes about 839. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it. The GFX100 II's pixel pitch works out to 43.8 mm across 11,648 pixels, or 3.76 micrometers.

articles.summary_long:
Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. Working across media, the artist intricately beads monumental works and incorporates a wide range of fabrics and materials. Jeffrey Gibson: A Real Love Thing at Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center delves into the cross-disciplinary breadth of the artist’s practice throughout the past decade.

Drawing on the early and continuing influence of music, the artist often integrates song lyrics into tapestry-like wall hangings and three-dimensional works. Music also inspired the title of the exhibition, which Gibson drew from a 1971 interview with soul artist Marvin Gaye, who described his seminal album What’s Going On by saying, “I think I’ve got a real love thing going. I love people, I love life, and I love nature, and I can’t see why other people can’t be like that.” Reflecting this sentiment, Gibson’s approach is a luminous celebration of Indigenous symbolism and traditional materials, such as jingle cones used in ceremonial garments, tipi poles, and glass beads that have coated bags, moccasins, and other apparel hand-crafted by Native Americans throughout the centuries.

The artist also posits a future full of hope, joy, acceptance, and, like Gaye, a love-above-all ethos. A Real Love Thing continues through March 13 at the Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C., where Gibson will present a talk as part of the esteemed Sam Gilliam Lecture series on November 12. And if you’re near Eugene, Oregon, the artist’s traveling solo exhibition They Teach Love is also on view through through March 7 at the University of Oregon.

articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft.

The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved.

After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth .

articles.summary_long:
Sony dévoile le Lytia 720 , un capteur de 50 Mpx destiné au module photo principal des smartphones, notamment de milieu de gamme. Au programme, selon Sony : jusqu’à deux fois moins de bruit numérique en basse lumière que son prédécesseur, et la vidéo 4K 60p en HDR . Le Lytia 720 succède au Lytia 700 , dont il reprend le format de type 1/1,56 pouce, soit environ 8 x 6 mm (17 fois moins de surface qu’un capteur plein format).

En basse lumière, chaque photosite ne recueille qu’un signal faible , si bien que le bruit numérique devient visible. Sony annonce jusqu’à 50 % de bruit aléatoire en moins qu’avec le Lytia 700. Côté plage dynamique, Sony se montre (très) ambitieux et annonce 100 dB, soit environ 16,6 IL .

En vidéo 4K 60p HDR, Sony se contente en revanche d’un HDR en une seule image . En vidéo, le capteur filme en 4K jusqu’à 120 fps , ou 60 fps en HDR. D’après l’électronicien nippon, cette combinaison de 4K 60 fps, de HDR et d’AF sur tous les pixels est inédite pour un capteur Lytia de ce format .

articles.title: Binance victime d'un vol de cryptomonnaies de 6,3 Md$
articles.summary: L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission.
articles.summary_short: L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission.
articles.summary_long:
L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Si aucune fuite de clés privées n'a été identifiée à ce stade, les investigations ont depuis mis au jour plusieurs points de compromission. Le montant dérobé dépasse largement celui du précédent grand vol de cryptomonnaies, estimé à 1,5 Md$ lors de l'attaque contre Bybit en février 2025.

D'après les premières investigations communiquées par Binance, l'attaque pourrait avoir commencé par la compromission de l'ordinateur portable d'un ingénieur DevOps de l'entreprise. Les sociétés spécialisées dans l'analyse de la blockchain, notamment TRM Labs et Chainalysis, ont établi des liens entre cette attaque et le groupe de pirates TraderTraitor, associé à la Corée du Nord. Ce groupe est déjà soupçonné d'être impliqué dans plusieurs opérations de vol de cryptomonnaies à grande échelle.

Face à l'ampleur de l'attaque, plusieurs acteurs majeurs de l'écosystème financier numérique ont rapidement réagi. Tether, Circle et Ripple ont notamment participé au gel d'une partie des actifs dérobés. Cependant, plusieurs milliards de dollars restent difficiles à récupérer, notamment lorsque les pirates convertissent les actifs en cryptomonnaies qui ne peuvent pas être gelées directement par un émetteur centralisé.

articles.title: Martian Polar Crater Ice Shifts with Seasonal Frost
articles.summary: The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps.
articles.summary_short: The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps.
articles.summary_long:
The planet Mars shares many landforms and weather patterns with the Earth, including changing seasons, volcanoes, canyons, dust storms and dust devils, and water ice. But one feature that Earth and Mars share among the eight planets in our solar system are polar ice caps. Both are one of each planetâs striking features, but the major difference is while Earthâs polar ice caps are both comprised of water, Marsâ north polar ice cap is only comprised of water while its southern polar ice cap is carbon dioxide.

But how does the north polar ice cap water ice change with the seasons compared to Earth, and what can this teach scientists about Marsâ climate history? As discussed in a recent study published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, the researchers challenged our understanding of ice deposits in Marsâ northern polar ice cap region. The researchers note that better understanding seasonal changes in polar ice cap deposits could help gain insights into long-term climate changes on the Red Planet.

For the study, the researchers analyzed images of 36 craters within the northern polar ice cap region of Mars. This study identifies seasonal changes in polar ice deposits while providing motivation for future modeling work that could help expand our understanding of localized climates on Mars. What new insights into Mars polar crater ice will researchers make in the coming years and decades?

articles.summary_long:
The dwarf planet Ceres is arguably one of the most overlooked and underappreciated planetary objects in the entire solar system. This could be because while Ceres has the same dwarf planet designation as Pluto, Ceres is largely considered an âasteroidâ since it resides the in main asteroid belt. For the study, researchers used a combination of Dawn spacecraft data and a series of computer models to examine the evolution of surface water ice and salt deposits on Ceresâ surface.

Specifically, this study focused on the transition of water ice to salt deposits through evaporation (scientifically called sublimation) and whether data collected from Dawn accurately estimated the amount of water ice and salt. In the end, the researchers found that the salt deposits might be hidden by the water ice deposits theyâre mixed with, with the salt deposits potentially existing in larger amounts than previously hypothesized, estimated to be between 30 to 50 percent greater. The finding resolves an existing paradox about how salt-rich deposits arise in the Ceres near-surface; they are likely not initially salt-rich but instead result from enrichment of salt at the optical surface by sublimation of salty ices.â Essentially, the salt-water ice deposits are sorted based on heat and evaporation, the salt within water ice mixture causes the water ice to evaporate faster, leaving behind the salt deposits.

This creates a feedback loop that results in different mixture amounts and types among separate water ice and salt deposits. Instead, they start out with low amounts of salt but have their salt contents increase from the evaporation of water ice that also contains salt. What new insights into Ceresâ salt deposits and water ice will researchers make in the coming years and decades?

articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. It depends on the night -- and the time. Outside of the Earth's atmosphere , the dark Moon , which shines by reflected sunlight, appears a magnificent ly brown-tinged gray.

The featured image highlights a collection of apparent colors of the full moon on Earth, documented by one astrophotographer over 10 years from different locations across Italy . A red - or yellow -colored moon usually indicates a moon seen near the horizon . A blue-colored moon is more rare and can indicate an atmosphere carrying larger dust particles .

What created the purple moon is unclear -- it may be a combination of several effects. articles.summary_short: The two men had never posed together, and the caption underneath called the picture a composite. To a picture editor, it meant two negatives combined.
articles.summary_long:
In the last stretch of the 1950 Maryland Senate race, roughly 300,000 copies of a four-page tabloid called From the Record went out across the state, and inside was a picture of Senator Millard Tydings standing close beside Earl Browder, the former head of the American Communist Party. The two men had never posed together, and the caption underneath called the picture a composite. What went into the Tydings picture were two real news photographs, and the Senate report is precise about them.

One was a 1938 photograph of Tydings, taken while he listened to election returns. The tabloid ran the word composite in the caption anyway. To a picture editor, it meant two negatives combined.

A composite disclosure is attached to a specific printed instance of an image. It does not tell you the picture is honest. If you sell a composite as a composite, say it in the visible caption, in the language a reader already speaks, and say what was combined.
