Wildlife files need more editing than most genres because they come from long lenses at high ISOs, subjects that won't pose, and backgrounds you couldn't choose. The edits that rescue those frames, such as cropping, noise reduction, and masked brightening, are the same ones that most often push a photo past the point where it looks natural. Matt Kloskowski sees it constantly when he reviews wildlife images.

Kloskowski calls it uncomfortable, which fits how your eye reacts when a wingtip or tail touches the edge. When an adjustment costs nothing to apply, the limit has to come from your eye, because your patience no longer sets one. Kloskowski lands around 50% to 60% as a starting point.

Pulling it lower lets noise creep back into dark backgrounds, which is where it tends to be worst. The background stays clean, and the subject gets some bite back. Kloskowski then moves to what he calls the sticker effect, where the subject is brightened, or the background darkened, until the animal looks pasted onto the scene with perfect edges.

The ghostly scene was photographed at Hverir , a geothermally active area found along northeastern Iceland's volcanic landscape . Triggered by solar activity , geomagnetic storms have unleashed energetic particles trapped in Earth's magnetic field. Penetrating the planet's upper atmosphere at high latitudes, the particles create auroral displays in the starry night sky.

Ghostly towers of steam and gas are venting from local fumaroles to dance against the eerie, greenish northern lights. For now, auroral activity on planet Earth remains in a high state as the Sun is only in early phases of decline from the peak of its solar activity cycle . articles.summary_long:
“ Everything Twice ” is a quiet meditation on disability and the ways we orient ourselves in the world. Since childhood, Cy Kuckenbaker noticed that one of his eyes drooped, something he attributed to a snowboarding accident. But doctors quickly dismissed that theory, and after innumerable tests and many, many years, the photographer learned he was born with a rare disease.

Kuckenbaker chronicles this realization alongside a slow, analog process he began to combat burnout. Utilizing homemade cameras crafted from cardboard boxes and drugstore magnifying glasses, he captured a variety of landscapes and sights on the West Coast. Pairing both the slow processes of labor-intensive photography with that of uncovering an unusual ailment creates a short film that’s equal part self-discovery and contemplation on disconnection and loss.

Astronomers using the Chandra X-ray Observatory (CXO) and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) zeroed in on a wispy-looking region of the Carina Nebula and found a ghostly looking cloud seemingly floating in isolation among the other clouds of gas and dust. Just in time for Halloween, although, it turns out that little cloud isn't the soul of a departed star. Instead, it's a region of the nebula that has been actively engaged in creating batches of hot, young new stars.

Credit: NASA/ESA/StSci The Carina complex is a huge diffuse nebula containing a collection of newborn stars nestled in a sea of starmaking gas and dust. It continues to produce new stars, many of them extremely bright and massive. A broad panorama of the Carina Nebula, a region of massive star formation in the southern skies.

This new method of determining the age of stars will help astronomers better understand the process of star formation. It's a dark and cold molecular cloud that covers about 7 light-years of space. At the same time, ionizing radiation from the nearby Eta Carina binary, as well as hot young stars, is eating away the materials in the cloud.

articles.summary_long:
The Cat's Head nebula gets its name from its appearance: it looks like a cat sitting so that it's facing away from the viewer, with its head turned around on the top of its neck, highlighted by a star that looks like a glowing eye. The unusual shape is made of gas and dust carved and formed by the radiation of young stars. Hubble's image of the Cat's Head is in visible light, while the JWST imaged it in both near and mid-infrared.

Each of the images shows a different aspect of the Cat's Head. The JWST, as an infrared telescope, presents different, yet no less gorgeous, images of the Cat's Head. Depasquale (STScI) Some of the turbulence in the gas, driven by the massive stars, appears more substantial in the JWST image.

A zoomed-in JWST NIR image of the head in the Cat's Head Nebula. Depasquale (STScI) In the JWST's mid-infrared image, the Cat's Head Nebula is transformed yet again. The white colour of the gas in this mid-infrared JWST image makes it look like Earthly clouds.

articles.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
articles.summary: In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here .
articles.summary_short: In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here .
articles.summary_long:
In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. As Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, Voyager 1 grabbed one more portrait of the solar system (excluding Mercury and Mars), including a final image of the pale blue dot we call home.

Did you know that a light-minute is a measure of distance, not time? At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna tracked Voyager 1 at 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles. You may have heard the term light-year in your favorite sci-fi movie or show, or when stargazing and referring to an object outside of our solar system.

This video best demonstrates the different distances between the inner solar system, outer solar system, and beyond, using light measurements. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here . You can get a real understanding of what a gravity assist might be like with our Gravity Assist activity and learn what it’s like to measure a “light minute” with our Measuring a Kid Minute activity guide!

The ice exposed on Vega and nearby islands indicates limited new snow accumulation over the winter, further reduced by sublimation and wind scouring, he said. “When entombed in snow and ice, the skull is preserved. But when exposed to melt, it weathers away, which will lead to a changing jawline and expanding eye socket.” The first comprehensive mapping of Vega Island’s ice was aided by Landsat imagery.

In a study published in 1982 , scientists described the island’s four ice caps with protruding rocky cliffs and outlet glaciers. Satellite images acquired in recent decades show ice loss from other glaciers on the island as well, with increased areas of exposed bedrock. articles.summary_long:
These past few years haven’t been kind to photography blogs. Many of the old classic websites have gone offline, and others have changed almost to the point of being unrecognizable. Photography Life has managed to weather the storm successfully for a few reasons.

It’s our way of holding our own against some much larger companies even in a declining industry. But I still hope that we can stick around a little longer and keep sharing our stories from the world of photography with you. If you’re wondering about ways to help Photography Life stay afloat, there is one thing which helps more than anything else, and that’s joining our Member Page .

It’s not just a way to help us; I think you’ll find that it’s a valuable resource for your own photography, no matter what level of photographer you are. And if it makes a difference, I enabled our planned Black Friday sale a month early so that you don’t feel like you’re getting a bad deal if you join. But no matter what happens, I am so grateful to have had these past ten years to share my love for photography with you.

articles.summary_long:
Viltrox has announced the AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro, a weather-sealed full frame prime for Sony E and Nikon Z with a 16-element optical design and voice coil autofocus. It costs $829 and joins the 50mm and 85mm f/1.4 Pro lenses, which gives Viltrox a set of three fast primes that comes in under $2,000 combined. In its launch announcement , Viltrox says the Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro stays sharp to the corners wide open, and it uses 16 elements in 11 groups to get there.

Viltrox says it kept focus breathing to a minimum, which matters for video and also makes the lens a good fit for focus stacking. The Sony version weighs about 760 g, and the Nikon version weighs about 780 g. The 35mm fills the last gap in Viltrox's full frame Pro line.

The AF 85mm f/1.4 Pro sells for $598 and the AF 50mm f/1.4 Pro for $549, so the three lenses add up to $1,976, and if you already own the 50mm, the 35mm uses the same PL-68A lens hood. If you shoot both stills and video, the click switch lets you choose between detents for stills and a smooth aperture ring for video, the voice coil motors keep focus noise down, and the low breathing keeps focus pulls from visibly zooming the frame. The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro for Sony E and the Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.4 Pro for Nikon Z are available now for $829.

articles.title: How Two Fluke Photos Revealed a Humpback Had Crossed the World
articles.summary: On August 22, 2022, Ekaterina Kalashnikova photographed a fluke off Fumba, in the Zanzibar channel, on the far side of the planet. Two frames prove that one whale was in two places on two dates.
articles.summary_short: On August 22, 2022, Ekaterina Kalashnikova photographed a fluke off Fumba, in the Zanzibar channel, on the far side of the planet. Two frames prove that one whale was in two places on two dates.
articles.summary_long:
On July 10, 2013, Natalia Botero-Acosta photographed a humpback whale's tail going down in the Gulf of Tribugá, on Colombia's Pacific coast. On August 22, 2022, Ekaterina Kalashnikova photographed a fluke off Fumba, in the Zanzibar channel, on the far side of the planet. No photo-identified adult male humpback has been logged across a greater great-circle distance between two breeding grounds, and no individual had previously been recorded alternating breeding grounds between the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

Among the longest separations previously documented between two humpback sightings was 11,261 kilometers, between the Mariana Islands and Mexico, with a year in between. An off-axis fluke often still matches, and a whale you photographed badly is worth more than a whale you did not photograph. The underlying finding deserved the attention, because a male crossing between the breeding stocks of two different ocean basins is genuinely extraordinary and nobody had documented it between these two.

The number 13,046 is a great-circle distance: the shortest path across a sphere between two coordinates where a camera happened to be pointing at this whale. Two frames prove that one whale was in two places on two dates. Working through 19,283 curated photo-ID images collected between 1984 and 2025, the team found two humpbacks that had been photographed in both eastern Australia and Brazil, moving in both directions.

articles.summary_long:
Soumyadeep Mukherjee is an award-winning astrophotographer from India. Hera photographed the asteroid pair on 18 October 2026 from about 1,280 kilometres away. Hera’s first resolved image shows that its Asteroid Framing Camera can separate the two objects as the spacecraft approaches.

Didymos measures about 780 metres across, while Dimorphos is approximately 151 metres wide. The smaller asteroid orbits Didymos at an average separation of roughly 1.15 kilometres. NASA launched the Double Asteroid Redirection Test, or DART, to test kinetic impact as an asteroid-deflection method.

The spacecraft struck Dimorphos on 26 September 2022, travelling at about 6.1 kilometers per second. Before the collision, Dimorphos took about 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit Didymos. ESA expects the first detailed images of Dimorphos on 25 November 2026.

articles.title: L’Institut pour la photographie de Lille rate le bicentenaire et repousse sa réouverture à 2030
articles.summary: Le grand lieu consacré à la photographie que la Région Hauts-de-France prépare à Lille devra encore attendre. Selon La Voix du Nord , l’ Institut pour la photographie ne rouvrira pas avant début 2030 .
articles.summary_short: Le grand lieu consacré à la photographie que la Région Hauts-de-France prépare à Lille devra encore attendre. Selon La Voix du Nord , l’ Institut pour la photographie ne rouvrira pas avant début 2030 .
articles.summary_long:
Le grand lieu consacré à la photographie que la Région Hauts-de-France prépare à Lille devra encore attendre. Selon La Voix du Nord , l’ Institut pour la photographie ne rouvrira pas avant début 2030 . Sa réouverture était d’abord prévue pour 2026 , l’année du bicentenaire de la photographie.

En juin, la Région a mis fin à sa collaboration avec l’agence Berger & Berger , chargée de la rénovation, en invoquant une « défaillance ». Le projet a aussi été revu à la baisse : l’Institut occupera environ 2 600 m² , contre 3 900 m² prévus jusqu’ici. La Région parle d’un simple « contretemps ».

Pour ne pas rater complètement le bicentenaire de la photographie , célébré jusqu’en septembre 2027, la Région prévoit d’ouvrir provisoirement un petit espace de 270 m² sur place. D’ici là, l’Institut continue de travailler hors les murs, notamment au Théâtre du Nord. Olivier Spillebout , fondateur de la Maison de la Photographie de Lille, dénonce depuis plusieurs années le coût d’une institution financée depuis 2018 sans véritable lieu ouvert au public .

The torrent of corona related discoveries keeps coming. Spicules are spike-like geysers of plasma that shoot up into the solar atmosphere at tens of kilometers per second, eventually collapsing back down towards the surface after a few minutes.

When they eventually break, those shock waves blast part of the atmosphere upward, creating giant âcurtainsâ of plasma thousands of kilometers into the Sunâs atmosphere. Video showing solar spicules, as seen by Hinode in 2007. One is created when magnetic field lines snap and break in the solar atmosphere.

CoSCos pull spicular sheet plasma back up from the surface into the corona, powering the solar wind and providing energy that heats the area. Gretchen Scherer ’s paintings of affluent homes, studios, and libraries appear to expand before our eyes. Brimming with ornately framed paintings installed salon-style on richly papered walls, her half-imagined spaces are inspired by real places, which she infuses with a playful brightness and whimsy. When we home in on one particular floral arrangement, framed artwork, or piece of furniture, it seems that there’s a sudden increase in how much more there is to explore.

Scherer’s new solo exhibition, In Time at Monya Rowe Gallery , continues the artist’s fascination with historical interiors, from art museums and drawing rooms to palatial halls and ecclesiastical spaces. The artist leans into a kind of escapism or longing for not only elegant, luminous surroundings but a desire to immerse oneself, quite literally, in the world of art. In our era of steel, glass, concrete, and contractor gray interiors, Scherer celebrates craftsmanship and beauty.

Fantastical convergences of art history and architecture occur in pieces like “A French Cafe with Paintings,” where a Beaux Arts interior transforms into an ad hoc gallery with myriad famous works casually strewn about. Working in oil, Scherer’s choice of media nods to the same used to create many of the historical examples she includes. In Time opens today and continues through January 9 in New York.

Taylor Waddell, who you might recognize from the OpenCAL layerless 3D printer , saw a BART gate and asked “why not?” It was largely constructed with a laser cutter at Jacob’s Makerspace at UC Berkeley, and features motorized doors and a working card reader. This is actually Waddell’s 2nd fare gate costume, built to reflect the changes in transit design since his earlier iteration. articles.summary_long:
Des données personnelles et des références de contrats ont été exposées, mais Engie assure que son système d'information interne et les données bancaires n'ont pas été compromis. Engie a alerté certains de ses clients français après avoir détecté des accès non autorisés à un outil utilisé par ses partenaires commerciaux pour prospecter et commercialiser ses offres d’électricité et de gaz. Révélé fin octobre 2026, l’incident porte sur des données personnelles et des informations contractuelles.

Les références des points de livraison d’électricité (PDL) et des points de comptage et d’estimation du gaz (PCE) figurent également parmi les informations exposées. Engie n’a précisé ni le nombre de clients concernés ni l’identité du partenaire dont l’outil a été compromis. L’incident concerne une plateforme utilisée par des partenaires commerciaux, et non directement les systèmes informatiques internes d’Engie.

Le groupe indique avoir interrompu les accès non autorisés. En s’appuyant sur des données personnelles et des références contractuelles exactes, des fraudeurs pourraient se faire passer pour des conseillers du fournisseur ou des techniciens afin d’obtenir des informations supplémentaires ou d’inciter les clients à effectuer des paiements frauduleux. Engie appelle ses clients à la vigilance face aux sollicitations inhabituelles.

articles.summary: Le groupe Blackhatsect0r affirme avoir dérobé les données de plus de 50 000 contacts et 114 214 documents PDF de La Mutuelle Communale. Les informations revendiquées comprennent notamment des numéros de Sécurité sociale, des adresses électroniques et des coordonnées bancaires.

articles.summary_long:
Le groupe Blackhatsect0r affirme avoir dérobé les données de plus de 50 000 contacts et 114 214 documents PDF de La Mutuelle Communale. Les informations revendiquées comprennent notamment des numéros de Sécurité sociale, des adresses électroniques et des coordonnées bancaires. Selon les chiffres rapportés le 27 octobre par le site Cyberattaque.org , les attaquants prétendent avoir récupéré 50 344 fiches de contacts et 114 214 documents PDF, représentant 46,6 Go de données.

Les données annoncées par les cybercriminels comprennent plusieurs catégories d’informations personnelles. BlackHatsect0r affirme notamment détenir 30 056 enregistrements de numéros de Sécurité sociale, dont 24 335 valeurs distinctes, ainsi que 17 812 enregistrements d’IBAN, dont 12 153 valeurs distinctes. Cyberattaque.org indique avoir examiné cinq extraits CSV de 1 000 enregistrements chacun, ainsi que plusieurs documents PDF.

Au-delà des données relatives aux adhérents, la revendication évoque plusieurs composants du système d’information. Selon le site Cyberattaque.org, Blackhatsect0r affirme proposer l’ensemble des données revendiquées à la vente pour 10 000€, avec un règlement en cryptomonnaie. La combinaison de coordonnées personnelles, de données bancaires et de documents administratifs pourrait faciliter des tentatives d’usurpation d’identité, de fraude documentaire ou d’hameçonnage ciblé.

articles.title: Avec le projet Lightwell, IBM et Red Hat gèrent les patchs des logiciels open source
articles.summary: Face à l'afflux attendu de correctifs de failles découvertes par l'IA sur les logiciels open source, IBM et Red Hat présentent le projet Lightwell. Cette plateforme combinant IA et expertise humaine sert de couche de coordination pour intégrer les patchs dans la supply chain logicielle des entreprises sans interruption de service.

articles.summary_long:
Face à l'afflux attendu de correctifs de failles découvertes par l'IA sur les logiciels open source, IBM et Red Hat présentent le projet Lightwell. Cette plateforme combinant IA et expertise humaine sert de couche de coordination pour intégrer les patchs dans la supply chain logicielle des entreprises sans interruption de service. Il revendiqué la découverte de plusieurs milliers de failles dans des applications open source.

Pour répondre à ces problématiques, IBM et sa filiale Red Hat viennent de présenter le projet Lightwell, doté d’un budget de 5 Md$ et mobilisant 20 000 ingénieurs des deux sociétés. L’objectif de l’initiative est de créer une plateforme pour accélérer la détection et la correction des vulnérabilités dans les logiciels open source. Aucune mise à niveau ni accès au code source n’est requis.

Les entreprises pourront partager des vulnérabilités sensibles sous embargo via un « modèle d'intermédiaire sécurisé » et recevoir des correctifs validés pour les plateformes Red Hat et le code de la communauté indépendante. Elles pourront également déployer des correctifs sur l'ensemble des chaînes de dépendances, signaler et résoudre les problèmes dans les environnements de production actifs, et partager les correctifs en amont afin que la communauté open source puisse les intégrer. « Nous voulons nous assurer que tous les correctifs que nous fournissons aux entreprises via la plateforme soient également mis à la disposition de la communauté open source qui a développé le code », explique Ashesh Badani, vice-président senior et directeur des produits chez Red Hat, à CSOonline .

articles.title: Apple partage le code source de son chiffrement post-quantique
articles.summary: En rendant public sur un répertoire GitHub les principes mathématiques qui sous-tendent sa vérification du chiffrement post-quantique, Apple met au défi l'ensemble du secteur de prouver que son propre code est sûr. Le chiffrement post-quantique d’Apple présente toutefois des limites.

Le chiffrement post-quantique d’Apple présente toutefois des limites.
articles.summary_long:
En rendant public sur un répertoire GitHub les principes mathématiques qui sous-tendent sa vérification du chiffrement post-quantique, Apple met au défi l'ensemble du secteur de prouver que son propre code est sûr. L'univers de la technologie prend rapidement conscience de la menace que représentent les futurs systèmes quantiques pour la sécurité au moment où ils seront capables de contourner facilement le chiffrement utilisé actuellement pour protéger sa présence sur Internet. Dans ce contexte, la décision d’Apple de partager le code de cryptographie post-quantique de l’iPhone et du Mac sur GitHub en dit long.

Les documents récemment publiés comprennent le code source de corecrypto, la bibliothèque cryptographique utilisée par le framework de sécurité d’Apple, CryptoKit et CommonCrypto. Cela fait des années que la firme à la pomme travaille sur la protection cryptographique post-quantique. Cette protection sécurise à la fois les conversations et leurs clés de chiffrement contre de futures attaques quantiques.

L’entreprise pense qu’en le publiant de cette manière, les chercheurs en sécurité pourront vraiment mettre ces protections à l'épreuve pour s'assurer qu'elles fonctionneront lorsque l'informatique quantique deviendra véritablement une menace. Le chiffrement post-quantique d’Apple présente toutefois des limites. Il est bon de voir qu’Apple continue ainsi de mettre en place des protections contre la menace imminente de l’informatique quantique.
